newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on wheat surge, cold snap.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on wheat surge, cold snap.

text.p: A limit-up surge in the neighboring wheat pit and forecasts for continued cold weather in the U.S. Midwest drove CBOT corn futures to a higher close, traders said.
"They're talking planting delays," a trader said. "The six- to 10-day was for below-average temperatures too."

Cold, wet weather in the northern U.S. Midwest plus serious flooding in portions of the Dakotas and Minnesota have slowed spring fieldwork and led to concerns about delays in seeding the corn crop. And Friday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook was for more of the same.
The NWS Friday said temperatures through the entire Midwest would be below- to much-below-normal April 17-21.
News U.S. exporters reported a sale of 101,600 tonnes of corn to Japan may have helped the bull's cause.

Little direction came from Monday's USDA weekly export inspections. USDA Monday said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended April 10 totaled 33.866 million bushels, within the range of expectations for 33 million to 38 million.
Corn closed one to 4-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 4-1/4 at $3.03-3/4 a bushel.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 85,000 contracts, below the 100,112 traded Friday.

Cargill Inc bought three million bushels of July and bought six million December, traders said. Merrill Lynch futures bought two million May, Refco Inc bought five million bushels of May and Smith Barney bought two million each of May and July, traders said.

In spread trading, Farmers Commodities Corp did two million bushels of July/December at 16 cents, premium July and R.J. O'Brien did one million bushels of July/May at 2-1/2 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 26,385 traded Friday.
